title: Adaptive color token mapping and legend virtualization for long time-series
creator: Ava Martinez
description: We need a cohesive approach to map design tokens to series colors across themes (light/dark/high-contrast) and to virtualize legend rendering for charts that have dozens-to-hundreds of series. This ticket covers token contracts for semantic series roles (primary/secondary/high-priority/threshold), a contrast-first fallback system for low-contrast series, legend virtualization + pinning UX, and perf-friendly sampling for tooltip/hover hit testing. Goal: provide accessible color defaults, keep per-chart CSS/JS minimal, and reduce rendering and interaction overhead for very large series sets.
acceptance_criteria: Token contract defined: semantic roles (series-01..series-12, series-accent, series-threshold, series-muted) with contrast targets for WCAG AA and APCA guidance
Implementation guide produced: mapping rules for light, dark, and high-contrast OS modes and explicit override precedence (user token > chart theme > runtime fallback)
Legend virtualization implemented: only visible legend items render in DOM; pinned items are sticky and preserved across virtualized scroll
UX: ability to 'pin' up to 5 series to the top of the legend; pinned items appear in the pinned region and maintain keyboard focus order
Accessibility: screen reader summary announces visible series count and pinned list; keyboard navigation cycles through pinned then virtualized items
Performance: charts with 200 series show no more than 5% CPU increase vs baseline for initial render and reduce long-press/hover hit-testing overhead by at least 60%
Automated visual tests: theme contrast checks and legend virtualization smoke tests added to CI (Chromatic and Lighthouse where applicable)
design_notes: Motivation: product teams occasionally load telemetry charts with many series (20-300). Current legend DOM growth causes layout thrash and keyboard/voiceover inefficiencies. Color choices also drift between themes and can fail contrast in dark/high-contrast modes.

Token approach: introduce semantic tokens rather than per-index color assumptions. E.g. series-primary, series-secondary, series-muted, series-accent, series-threshold. These map to palette tokens at theme time and include contrast-aware fallbacks computed near runtime if necessary.

Contrast strategy: prefer color pairs that meet WCAG AA for normal text at default chart sizes. When a series color fails contrast in a theme, the runtime will apply a minor luminance shift or a subtle-outline treatment rather than arbitrary reassigning which would break color semantics across customers.

Legend virtualization: use list virtualization (windowing) with fixed item height; pinned area is rendered above the virtualized window as a separate non-virtualized region. Maintain stable keys so pinned/unpinned operations don't reflow items unnecessarily.

Hit-testing perf: avoid per-point expensive checks by maintaining an aggregated downsampled interaction layer: a sparse spatial index sampled at 1-2% of points for hover/hit detection and fallback to KD-tree lookup for precise proximity only when needed.

Trade-offs: runtime color adjustments add a slight inconsistency with exported SVGs if colors are adjusted client-side; we will document this and provide a prerender pass for export endpoints. Virtualization introduces complexity for in-legend search and focus management which we mitigate by shallow aria-live updates and a clear keyboard model (tab to legend, arrow within, P to pin/unpin).

Design alternatives considered: (1) server-side color normalization (rejected for developer friction), (2) single-pass legend pagination (rejected for discoverability), (3) force-contrast by always desaturating low-contrast series (rejected for data misinterpretation risk).

notes_for_engineering: Expose token mapping as JSON manifest on the design-system package so runtime consumers can compute fallbacks without hardcoding palettes.
Provide an opt-in config flag chartConfig.enableLegendVirtualization defaulting to false for gradual rollout behind feature flag.
Include a small JS utility to compute minimal luminance adjustments that preserve hue; prefer CSS custom properties for theme injection where possible.
